name: Bicycle Safety Checklist
description: A pre-ride safety routine covering the ABC quick check, helmet fit, lights, visibility and road rules for safe cycling.

items.text: Check tire air pressure and inflate to the sidewall range
Confirm both brakes grip firmly and release cleanly
Check the chain is on, lubricated and shifts cleanly
Verify quick-releases or axles are closed and tight
Lift and drop the bike to listen for loose parts
Wear a helmet that sits level and fits snugly
Buckle the chin strap and check the side straps form a V
Replace any helmet that has been crashed or damaged
Consider gloves for grip and protection
Wear closed shoes that grip the pedals
Fit a white front light and red rear light
items.note: Required at night in most places and useful by day

items.text: Check reflectors are present and clean
Wear bright or reflective clothing
Confirm lights are charged before night rides
Clean any mirrors and adjust for a clear view
Set saddle height for a slight knee bend at the bottom
Check handlebars and stem are tight and aligned
Confirm you can reach and operate both brake levers
Make sure a bell or horn is fitted if required
Adjust the saddle and bars for a comfortable position
Ride in the same direction as traffic
Obey traffic signals, signs and lane markings
Signal turns and stops with hand signals
Stay alert at intersections and driveways
Keep both hands ready to brake and avoid distractions
Follow local helmet and equipment laws, which vary by region
Plan a route with safer roads or bike lanes
Check the weather and dress for conditions
Carry a spare tube, pump and basic tools
Bring water, ID and a phone
Lock plans or let someone know longer routes

faq.q: What is the ABC Quick Check?
faq.a: ABC stands for Air, Brakes and Chain, and Quick refers to quick-releases or axles. It is a fast pre-ride routine: check tire air, confirm brakes work, make sure the chain is on and running, and verify wheels are secure before you ride.

faq.q: How should a bike helmet fit?
faq.a: A helmet should sit level, about two finger-widths above the eyebrows, snug but not tight, with the straps forming a V under each ear and a buckled chin strap. It should not rock side to side. Replace any helmet after a crash.

faq.q: Do I need lights in the daytime?
faq.a: A white front light and red rear light are essential at night and in low light, and many riders use them in daylight too for extra visibility. Add reflectors and bright or reflective clothing so drivers see you sooner.

faq.q: What road rules should cyclists follow?
faq.a: Ride in the same direction as traffic, obey signals and signs, signal turns, use bike lanes where available and stay predictable. Local laws on helmets, sidewalks and equipment vary by region, so check the rules where you ride.

faq.q: Can I print this bicycle safety checklist?
faq.a: Yes. Print it or download the PDF so you can keep it by the door and run the ABC quick check, helmet fit and visibility steps before each ride.
